Every time we build a website, I use SE Ranking to find quick wins and prove to new clients that we can reach their goals. Read more 1 / 3 See the full scope of what SE Ranking’s API covers See product tour FAQ Q What is an SEO API? A An SEO API gives teams programmatic access to SEO data, including keyword rankings, backlinks, domain metrics, site audits, and competitor insights. This means you can assess that information without going through the platform interface manually. Instead, you can pull data directly into your own tools, or connect via SEO MCP to access it from inside an AI assistant. Show more Show less Q Why is it ideal to use an API for SEO? A For agencies and teams working at scale, manual data collection creates a bottleneck. You need to log in, export files, connect them with other sources, and repeat the process across multiple clients. An API removes those steps. Data flows directly into your dashboards, analytics platforms, CRMs, and BI tools without manual intervention at each stage. It also means running analyses at a volume that manual work can’t match. Show more Show less Q What SEO data can I access with this API? A SE Ranking’s API is structured across two layers. The Data API covers keyword research, backlink analysis, domain performance, SERP data, site audits, and AI visibility research. The Project API lets you manage and automate SEO workflows within the platform, including rank tracking, keyword grouping, and competitor monitoring at the project level. All data is returned as structured JSON. Show more Show less Q Is SE Ranking’s API data accurate? A Yes, SE Ranking’s API pulls from its large database and real-time analysis to provide accurate data. It collects and updates new SEO data daily, with a database that employs in-depth tracking to cover global and local search results. It also uses a vast link index to provide accurate data on backlinks. Show more Show less Q What are the limitations? A A few things worth knowing before you integrate. SE Ranking doesn’t currently offer first-party SDKs and integration is done via the REST API reference and a Postman collection for endpoint testing. Also, default requests-per-second limits are lower than some competitors’, though these can be increased by contacting the support team. If you’re migrating from another API provider, you’ll need to remap your endpoints Show more Show less Q How do I access SE Ranking’s API? A Accessing our API is straightforward. Just log in to your SE Ranking account, navigate to the API tab under the Settings section, and retrieve your unique API key. Once you have your API key, you can use it for different purposes. For more information, refer to our API documentation. Show more Show less Q How do I get an SE Ranking API key? A API is included with every SE Ranking subscription. To get your key, log in to your SE Ranking account, go to the API section. From there, you can copy your API key and use it to integrate SE Ranking’s data into your applications, dashboards, or reports. Show more Show less Q What is the cost of API access? A API access comes with any SE Ranking plan (Core at $129/mo and Growth at $279/mo). You can even test it in the free trial account. For higher volume, the API Add-On starts at $149/month and can be added to any existing subscription. Pay-as-you-go is also available with a $50 minimum deposit. Show more Show less Q Can I use this API without technical expertise? A Yes, you don’t need a development team to use the SE Ranking’s API. One method is to run a pre-written code in Google Colab to gather data, then apply specific formulas within Google Sheets to clean the results. Use our code as an example and adjust it as needed. MCP is another path. Once connected, you can query keyword rankings, backlink data, site audit results directly from Claude, Codex, Cursor, or any MCP-compatible AI assistant in plain language. No code required. Show more Show less Q What is an MCP server? A MCP is a bridge between AI models like Claude and external tools, data sources, and services. SE Ranking’s MCP server connects SE Ranking’s data directly to AI assistants like Claude, Codex, Gemini, Cursor, and any other client. Once connected, you can query keyword rankings, backlink data, site audits, and more in plain language, without switching between tools or writing code. Show more Show less Q How does MCP differ from the API? A API and MCP server serve different use cases. The API gives you programmatic access to SE Ranking’s data for building custom integrations, automated workflows, and data pipelines. The MCP server is for querying SE Ranking data conversationally from inside an AI assistant. You can run research, analyses, and AI-assisted workflows without switching context. Both are included in every SE Ranking plan. codes Authentication Subscription Get subscription details API API rate limits API rate limits To ensure the stability, performance, and fair usage of the SE Ranking platform, API rate limits restrict the number of requests an application can make within a given timeframe. Limits are enforced at the API key level , meaning all requests made with the same key—across threads, workers, or servers—are counted together. SE Ranking evaluates request rates using a rolling one-second window , continuously measuring traffic over the immediately preceding second. Standard rate limits Different rate limits apply to the Data API and the Project API: API Use case Limit (per API key) Data API Retrieving raw data (e.g., keywords, backlinks, domain analysis, website audit, AI Search). 10 requests per second (RPS) Project API Managing account resources (e.g., adding or deleting websites, managing keywords, updating settings). 5 requests per second (RPS) Trial accounts During the trial period, the Data API has a default rate limit of 1 request per second (RPS) . If your evaluation requires higher throughput, this limit can be increased upon request. Do not treat a 429 error as a permanent failure, and do not immediately retry the request. 1. Exponential Backoff with Jitter The industry-standard strategy for handling rate limiting is implementing exponential backoff with jitter . Exponential Backoff: Increase the delay between retries exponentially after each failed attempt (e.g., wait 1 second, then 2s, then 4s, then 8s). Jitter: Add a small amount of randomization to the delay interval. This is critical to prevent the “thundering herd” problem, where multiple clients become synchronized and attempt to retry simultaneously, immediately causing another rate limit violation. 2. Client-side throttling We recommend implementing client-side monitoring and request throttling. Proactively managing your request frequency to stay within the defined limits is more efficient than relying solely on error handling. 3. Simple delays (caution) Because the SE Ranking API uses a rolling one-second window, a brief pause (e.g., 200-500 milliseconds) might be sufficient for occasional, isolated overages.
